questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Move back to your lane when you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Move back to the right side of the road right away.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move back to your lane when you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, move back to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the car you passed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Hunting area.
State park.
Deer crossing.
Wildlife preserve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph may take up to ____ to stop completely.

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Trucks stop much slower than cars at the same speed. A fully loaded truck may need almost 400 feet to stop at 55 mph.

questions.question: Your body removes approximately:

options.text: Three alcoholic drinks per hour.
One alcoholic drink per hour.
Two alcoholic drinks per hour.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One alcoholic drink per hour.
questions.explanation: The average person's body processes about one drink per hour. How impaired you become depends on many factors: the amount you drink, how fast you drink it, your weight, what you have eaten, and your health.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow on a traffic signal, you should:

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow points to.
Slow down and stop, if you can do so safely.
Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
You have the right of way, and oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: You are driving in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. You should:

options.text: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. Always check your mirrors and use your turn signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Cause too much oil to be used.
Require a tune-up sooner than normal.
Make you sleepy while driving.
Start grass fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you sleepy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases from the engine. Fumes from a leaky exhaust can cause death quickly. They can also make you drowsy while driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway ahead.
You are driving over a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guard rail.

questions.question: Your ability to stop is affected by:

options.text: Traffic lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
Road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect your ability to stop. Slow down when roads are wet, icy, or slippery so you can control your vehicle. Driving too fast on bad roads puts you at risk if you need to stop.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Other drivers can follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with a single rider.
You must move completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
A motorcycle's brake lights turn on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must move completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane of space. Move your entire vehicle into the left lane before passing a motorcycle on the left.

questions.question: Your vehicle stops slower when stopping on:

options.text: Wet or icy roads.
Paved highways.
Roads at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wet or icy roads.
questions.explanation: Stopping takes longer on wet or icy roads. Stopping also takes longer on loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Have large blind spots.
Stop faster than cars.
Need the same space to turn as cars.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have blind spots in front, on the sides, and in the back. Do not stay in these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than cars because of their size and weight.

questions.question: A speed restriction sign:

options.text: Can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
Has a triangle shape.
Is blue with black letters.
Shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.
questions.explanation: Signs for curves and turns often show a recommended speed for that area. You should obey this speed in all weather conditions, even in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow center line. You know this road is:

options.text: A two-way road.
A one-way road.
Under repair.
Requiring you to stay left of the yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: A two-way road.
questions.explanation: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street. You must:

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic ahead.
Lanes are shifting.
Low overhead clearance.
A new lane is being added.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns that traffic may come from the opposite direction.

questions.question: Leave more space than usual between your car and the one ahead when stopped:

options.text: On a hill.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your car when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving, the extra space reduces the chance of a collision.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. You should:

options.text: Signal with your wheels turned left.
Signal with your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so other drivers let you through.
Drive around a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal with your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If a car hits you from behind, straight wheels prevent you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: It is important to watch for motorcycles because:

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use headlights.
Riders are less skilled than other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to spot than cars. They can hide in a car's blind spot. It is difficult to judge distance and speed. Always be alert and cautious around motorcycles.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb when parking uphill. If your car rolls, it will roll into the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: Which of the following is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Maintain a constant speed throughout the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Gradually speed up as you exit. Speeding up while entering a curve makes your car harder to control.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you can check your blind spots by:

options.text: Using the inside rearview mirror.
Using the outside rearview mirror.
Using both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to look over your shoulder before every lane change. This is the best way to check your blind spots.

questions.question: You are driving and hear a siren. You cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down. Don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but cannot see where it is coming from, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you know the emergency vehicle is not headed toward you.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing without flashing warning signals or crossing gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing.
questions.explanation: Be ready to stop and let any train pass. Do not cross until you see that no trains are coming and your entire vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing the tracks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road narrows ahead.
There are a series of curves ahead.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are a series of curves ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road has three or more curves coming up.

questions.question: You may cross solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: You can cross broken lines, but not solid lines. The only time you may cross a solid yellow line is when you are turning.

questions.question: When parking your vehicle downhill on a two-way street:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road when parking downhill. If your car rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: If you are turning onto a street with more than one lane in your direction, you should:

options.text: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.
Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.
Turn into the middle lane.
Turn into any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you were just in. Do not change lanes while you are turning.

questions.question: What is a "No zone?"

options.text: A designated no passing zone
A one-way traffic area
The blind spot of a large vehicle
An area designated for motor vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot of a large vehicle
questions.explanation: "No zones" are the large blind spots around trucks and big vehicles. Stay out of these areas where the truck driver cannot see you.
